homepage_top_label: AI FOR SCIENCE IN SYSTEMS MEDICINE

biography.en: Ge Zhang is a clinician-scientist working at the intersection of AI for Science, systems medicine, and translational biomedicine. His research integrates explainable artificial intelligence, multimodal clinical data, and multi-omics profiling to resolve disease heterogeneity, uncover mechanistic determinants, and translate molecular signatures into clinically actionable knowledge across major chronic diseases. Cardiovascular disease, particularly atherosclerosis, represents a major disease context in his research, with specific interests in the vascular microenvironment, vascular smooth muscle cell plasticity, and circadian disruption. His work spans population-scale clinical modeling, multimodal and multi-omics integration, computational inference, mechanistic interrogation, and translational validation, establishing cross-scale links from molecular and cellular states to clinical phenotypes and disease outcomes.
biography.zh: 张格（Ge Zhang），临床医学与计算生物医学研究者，主要从事 AI for Science、系统医学与转化生物医学研究。其研究面向重大慢性疾病，融合可解释人工智能、多模态临床数据与多组学研究体系，旨在解析疾病异质性、识别关键机制驱动因素，并推动分子特征向具有临床意义的生物学认知与转化标志物延伸。 心血管疾病，尤其是动脉粥样硬化，是其重要疾病研究场景，重点关注动脉粥样硬化血管微环境、血管平滑肌细胞可塑性及昼夜节律紊乱。 其研究贯穿人群尺度临床建模、多模态与多组学整合、计算推断、机制解析与转化验证，致力于建立从分子与细胞状态到临床表型及疾病结局的跨尺度关联。

description: Ge Zhang is a clinician-scientist and computational medicine researcher at Zhengzhou University working at the intersection of AI for Science, systems medicine, and translational medicine. His research integrates multimodal clinical data, artificial intelligence, multi-omics, and single-cell approaches to study major chronic diseases. His principal research interests include cardiovascular and atherosclerotic disease, circadian disruption, vascular biology, vascular smooth muscle cell plasticity, and mechanism-guided translational discovery.
disambiguating_description: Ge Zhang (张格) is a clinician-scientist and computational medicine researcher affiliated with Zhengzhou University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. This profile refers to the researcher whose work spans AI for Science, systems and translational medicine, multimodal clinical data, multi-omics and single-cell research, with a major focus on cardiovascular and atherosclerotic disease, circadian disruption, vascular biology, and vascular smooth muscle cell plasticity. His broader research portfolio includes cross-disease computational and systems medicine studies across major chronic diseases, including cancer-related research.
